The acne medication isotretinoin is a vitamin A analog, and 
exposed infants are at extremely high risk for fetal anomalies 
and miscarriages. Women should stop its use for at least 
1 month before conception. Beta-carotene is not associated 
with birth defects. Although no cases have been seen, theoreti-
cally someone eating liver could consume as much preformed 
vitamin A as has been associated with fetal anomalies, so large 
amounts of liver, liver pâté, and liverwurst or braunschweiger 
are not recommended in the first trimester.
Vitamin D.  ​According to the IOM, vitamin D requirements 
do not increase during pregnancy; intakes of 600 IU/day 
(15 mcg/day) are sufficient when considering bone health. The 
few dietary sources of vitamin D are salmon and other fatty 
fish, as well as some fortified breakfast cereals and mushrooms 
exposed to UV light. Not all dairy products are fortified, but 
liquid milk (if sold interstate) is a good source, usually contain-
ing 100 IU/8 oz (see Appendix Table 51 and Clinical Insight: 
Vitamin D: How Much Sun is Needed?).
